title: Tenali and the Wicked Astrologer

full_text:
A gloomy, manipulative court astrologer named Bhairava Shastri, who sought to dominate King Krishnadevaraya through fear, arrived at the court with a dark, ominous parchment.
He prostrated himself before the throne, trembling with theatrical dread:
'Alas, Emperor Krishnadevaraya! The stars have aligned in a catastrophic conjunction!
Saturn and Mars have entered your house of life!
The planetary omens reveal that within thirty days, Your Majesty shall suffer an incurable, fatal affliction—unless you perform an imperial penance, surrender your royal signet ring to the temple council, and donate fifty thousand gold coins to my astrological academy!'

King Krishnadevaraya, devout and fearful of celestial wrath, turned pale. A heavy dread gripped the Emperor’s heart, and he fell into despair.

Tenali Raman stepped forward, his eyes flashing with sharp indignation at the charlatan’s cruel manipulation.
Tenali bowed to the King:
'Maharaj, before we surrender the empire’s treasury and signet ring, let us verify the infallible accuracy of the Pandit’s astrological foresight.'

Tenali turned to the astrologer, holding a sharp iron stylus in his hand:
'Revered Astrologer, your knowledge of planetary movements across the heavens is truly astonishing.
Tell me: does your chart reveal the exact hour, minute, and manner of your own death?'

The astrologer, eager to demonstrate total mastery over fate, puffed out his chest and boasted:
'Of course! My celestial horoscope is completely charted!
I am destined to live for another forty years in robust health, dying peacefully in my sleep at the ripe age of ninety-two, surrounded by my grandchildren!'

The moment the words left the astrologer’s lips, Tenali Raman drew the King’s ceremonial scimitar from its scabbard with a lightning flash of steel!
He placed the cold, razor-sharp blade gently against the astrologer’s trembling throat!

Tenali smiled with cold, terrifying amusement:
'Maharaj! Order the executioner to take this scimitar and sever this man’s head this very second!
If he dies right now on this carpet at the age of fifty-two, his horoscope was a fraudulent lie, and Your Majesty has nothing to fear from his thirty-day prophecy!
And if his horoscope was true, the sword will magically turn to flowers, so he has nothing to lose!'

The terrified astrologer shrieked in horror, fell to the floor, wet his robes in absolute panic, and babbed frantically:
'Mercy, Tenali! Mercy, Your Majesty! Do not strike!
My horoscope was a lie! The stars predicted no doom!
I forged the prophecy to terrify the King into granting gold and influence to my academy!'

King Krishnadevaraya sprang to his feet, his fear instantly transformed into righteous fury and profound relief!
The King ordered the fraudulent astrologer stripped of all titles and banished from Vijayanagara forever.
The Emperor embraced Tenali Raman with tears of gratitude:
'Tenali, thy fearless wit has broken the chains of fear that bound my spirit!'
The court celebrated Tenali as the champion of courage, demonstrating that superstition vanishes when confronted by bold reason.
moral: Charlatans who predict the doom of others to manipulate power are undone when asked about their own fate.
